vignette:
John, a 77-year-old delivery driver, sits in the therapy office, absorbing the warm afternoon light filtering through the blinds. His weathered hands rest on his thighs, fingers nervously tapping a rhythm that belies the calm facade he tries to maintain. The therapist notes the way he occasionally glances at the door, the twitch in his jaw tightening as it creaks open and shut.

John has been married to his wife, Linda, for over fifty years. They raised three children together, and he often reminisces about the joyful chaos of family life. Yet, beneath the surface of this seemingly contented life lies a darkness that has been growing since the assault that changed everything.

It happened two years ago on a routine delivery. John had just finished dropping off a load of supplies at a local grocery store in the early evening when he noticed a group of teenagers loitering near his truck. At first, he thought nothing of it. He had spent decades on the road, and he was accustomed to the occasional rowdy crowd. But as he returned to his vehicle, he felt a prickling sense of unease. 

Suddenly, one of the boys shouted at him, demanding money. John’s heart raced as he faced the group, their faces obscured by the shadows of the setting sun. He instinctively reached for his phone, thinking to call for help, but before he could react, he was surrounded. The fear coursed through him like ice water; he had never encountered such aggression in all his years.

The memory of that night haunts him. John recalls feeling the sharp jabs of fists against his ribs, the taste of blood in his mouth, and the echoing laughter that followed him as they fled. In the aftermath, he spent days replaying the incident over and over, grappling with a sense of vulnerability he had never felt before. He had always thought of himself as strong, a protector of his family, but now he felt stripped bare, exposed in a world that had turned dangerous.

Since that night, John’s life has become a series of battles against his own mind. His once simple task of delivering packages has become fraught with anxiety. He dreads the moments before he climbs into his truck, scanning the streets for familiar faces and potential threats. The familiar routes that once brought him peace now feel like a minefield, each turn a reminder of his past trauma. He has taken to avoiding certain neighborhoods entirely, and Linda has noticed the change in him.

At home, John feels the weight of unspoken words. He tries to maintain a brave face, but Linda knows something is wrong. When he comes home from work, she often finds him sitting in silence, staring out the window, lost in thought. The laughter and warmth that once filled their home have been replaced by an awkward tension. While he tries to engage in conversation, John finds himself responding with terse words, often cutting off discussions about anything that might lead back to his feelings.

Sleep is a stranger to him now. Nights are filled with vivid nightmares where the boys return, shadows looming, fists raised. He wakes up in a cold sweat, heart pounding, unable to shake the feeling that danger is lurking just outside the bedroom door. Linda often finds him pacing the living room, searching for solace that never arrives, her heart aching for the man she loves.

In therapy, John begins to share pieces of his story, describing the sense of betrayal that accompanies the assault—how he feels he has lost control not only of his safety but also of his identity. The conversations are challenging. He struggles to articulate the depth of his pain, but there is a flicker of hope when he sees a glimmer of understanding in the therapist’s eyes.

Yet, each session brings up memories he wishes to forget. He grapples with the reality that he is not the same man who drove those streets with confidence. The laughter of his grandchildren, once a source of joy, now brings tears to his eyes as he fears passing on his anxieties to them. The world outside feels both familiar and foreign, and he questions if he will ever feel safe again.

As he continues to grapple with the shadows of his past, John clings to the love of his wife and the support of his family. They are his anchors, grounding him in moments where he feels he might drift away into the darkness of his experience. In this therapeutic space, he seeks to reclaim the life he once knew, inch by inch, day by day.
